newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end a touch higher after narrow trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end a touch higher after narrow trade.

text.p: Greek stocks managed to settle marginally higher after trading in negative territory for most of the session with trading volume improving but still on the low side.

"Looking longer term, the market will climb higher on falling inflation and interest rates. However, the benchmark index needs help from construction shares, a wealth effect and a psychological boost from a rebound in the construction sector," said Nikos Verras, director of private banking at Interbank.
He said a rally in construction stocks sparked by the start of key infrastructure projects would fuel a sustained recovery in the market.
He liked shares of Metka, Maillis and thought construction shares Aktor, Hellenic Technodomiki, GEK and Michaniki were a good sectoral play.
Meanwhile, farmers continued a seven-day blockade of major highways protesting against Greece's austere 1997 budget and vowing to spend the Christmas holidays by the roadblocks.

They are demanding lower diesel fuel prices, cuts in the VAT tax on farm equipment, rescheduling of 1.3 billion drachmas of debt by farm cooperatives to state banks and higher price supports especially for cotton.
Socialist Prime Minister Costas Simitis, back from Lisbon, will announce his position on how to face the protest after a cabinet meeting on Wednesday.
Greece cut the marker 12-month T-bill rate by 50 basis points down to 11.50 percent in December. The issue came to market on Monday and sold well.
And Alpha Credit Bank on Tuesday joined Xiosbank other commercial banks announcing a 50 basis point cut in its savings deposit rates effective December 9.

The Athens general share index closed up 0.03 percent or 0.28 points higher at 916.99 from Tuesday's 916.71 close after opening at 916.50. Turnover rose to 4.4 billion drachmas on volume of 1.8 million shares, helped by block trades in National Bank.
